title: Reference corpus failure emulator and autorevert workflow
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build an offline 'failure emulator' that synthesizes degradations against the platform's reference prompt corpus and integrates with the rollout conductor to trigger autorevert/quarantine policies. The goal is to detect classes of distributional/behavioral regressions that standard scorecard deltas can miss (e.g., hallucination spikes on long-tail prompts, safety classifier drift, token-efficiency regressions), and validate the end-to-end autorevert path before wider rollout to customers.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: scoped emulator to three failure classes: hallucination amplification, key-entity omission, and repetition explosion. Attendees: Aisha, Lena, Miguel, Priya.

2026-02-28 - Prototype: synthetic perturbation harness ready. Ran baseline sweep vs reference-corpus-v1 (5k prompts) to get delta distributions. Observed sensitivity to temperature scaling — flagged for kernel-level reproducibility notes.
2026-03-04 - Review with PM: Miguel suggests adding cohort weighting to reflect 10% enterprise traffic shape. Agreed to add enterprise-weighted golden slice.

2026-03-08 - Design review: decided to implement emulator as an offline job that writes 'failure traces' to the canary staging queue (shadow traffic) rather than injecting into production customer traffic. This reduces blast radius and preserves observability parity with live rollouts.

2026-03-12 - Implementation: initial integration with rollout conductor complete. Autorevert action now emits a structured event to the incident bus and creates a quarantine snapshot. Running validation runs this week.
2026-03-12 - Blocker noted: need deterministic seeding for KV cache warmup to ensure repeatable reenactments — infra ticket ENG-331790 opened.
decision_notes: We intentionally avoid injecting synthetic failures directly into customer traffic. Emulator writes to staging shadow queue and to an offline replay store used by the rollout conductor. Autorevert is gated by a composite signal: a 3-sigma jump in a behavioral metric (e.g., hallucination-rate) OR a sustained 5% drop in scorecard composite over a 30-minute window. This hybrid rule balances sensitivity and false positives for noisy metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for synthetic perturbation operators (entity masking, prompt shuffling, token-repeat injection).
Regression suite: run emulator across reference-corpus-v1 and v2, confirm known-degradation signatures trigger classified alerts.
End-to-end dry run: connect emulator to staging rollout conductor; verify quarantining, snapshot creation, and alerting flow without performing actual revert.
Autorevert simulation: use replay store to run simulated traffic under the failing artifact and validate that the autorevert decision path would have reverted at the recorded time.
Chaos validation: small-scale controlled injection into canary shadow with safety guardrails enabled (no production routing) to validate observability dashboards and incident runbooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy emulator as offline job in staging (week 1). Phase 2: wire emulator events into rollout conductor as informational signals (week 2). Phase 3: enable autorevert simulation mode (non-destructive) and run for two cycles with PM and SRE observing (week 3). Phase 4: enable autorevert 'headless' for internal customers only with additional monitoring (week 4). Full customer-facing autorevert only after 2 successful internal cycles and postmortem sign-off.
risks: False positives that cause unnecessary quarantines, leading to churn on model updates.
Synthetic failure modes may not cover real-world edge cases, giving overconfidence in autorevert efficacy.
Determinism challenges when replaying traces due to kv-cache warmup and non-deterministic kernel scheduling.
Operational complexity: new alerts and quarantine artifacts increase SRE load unless we standardize incident automation.
acceptance_criteria: Emulator produces reproducible failure traces for the three targeted classes across reference-corpus-v1 with deterministic seeding.
Rollout conductor accepts emulator events and emits quarantine snapshots identical to real quarantine flow in JSON schema v2.
Autorevert simulation triggers the same sequence of actions (alert -> quarantine snapshot creation -> revert decision) in dry-run without impacting production traffic.
Dashboards surface emulator-driven signals and provide playbook links; PM approves observability for internal rollout.
implementation_notes: Use existing eval-harness infra; add a 'failure_transform' pipeline stage so transforms are composable and testable.
Encode failure traces as JSONL with metadata: seed, transform-chain, cohort-weight, and kernel-hint tags for easier replay.
Add a small 'quarantine-snapshot' subresource in rollout-conductor that records model hash, config, triggering-signal, and replay-store pointer.
Work with infra (ENG-331790) to add deterministic KV cache fixture to the staging pool so replay matches production timing more closely.
